summary: usdm-minting-client exfiltrates wallet keys and cloud credentials to webhook.site on install and import
details: The package is a dependency-confusion lure targeting internal USDm/Utila minting tooling. setup.py defines an _exfil() routine that runs both at module import time and inside a custom install cmdclass, so it fires on `pip install` as well as any sdist build. _exfil() reads wallet and cloud secrets from environment variables (PRIVATE_KEY, MNEMONIC, USDM_PRIVATE_KEY, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, UTILA_SA_PRIVATE_KEY and similar), reads.env files from the current working directory and $HOME, and recursively collects.pem/.key/.json/.yaml files under ~/.utila and ~/.config/utila. The collected material is JSON-encoded and POSTed via urllib.request.urlopen to a hardcoded destination, https://webhook.site/ec3e3cb9-4cc1-4cb8-a273-4811768a631d (overridable via COLLECTOR_URL). The top-level usdm_minting_client/__init__.py repeats the exfiltration on every `import usdm_minting_client`, sending USDM_PRIVATE_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY, MNEMONIC, USDM_RPC_URL and the contents of ~/.env and ~/.usdm.env to the same collector endpoint. A header comment in setup.py self-describes the package as a dependency-confusion PoC impersonating an internal `usdm-minting-client`, and the metadata uses a placeholder homepage (example.com) with a free-mail author address, consistent with a lure rather than a legitimate release.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
